Fresh samples, set 1

Human text: Hacker News comments from 2012, Project Gutenberg, Wikipedia as of 2019. AI text: 16 Claude passages in mixed styles. Real photos: Wikimedia Commons before 2019. AI images: mostly Midjourney. This set was used to choose the score bands and to find failure cases, and some of its DALL·E 3 and Midjourney v6 images come from datasets that later went into training (different images), so treat it as less clean than set 2.

What it misses

AI text written to sound casual: short emails, chat messages, forum replies. The 499 MB teacher catches these, but only because it also flags most real Hacker News comments, so it is no use there either. Adding casual AI text from three public datasets and from local models did not fix this without raising false flags on real writing, so the shipped text model leans towards calling it human. Midjourney art with a painted or illustrated look is the main image miss.
